name: moorings
topic: two moorings photographed an hour apart, and a claim about which is held more tightly
why_this_fixture: The INTELLIGENCE-002C rehearsal shape: a user hypothesis that arrives already claiming the
picture shows it, several image readings of very different quality, a comparison Semant
elected to draw, four candidate relations with four different fates, and a capability the
It exists to prove that nine specific dishonesties are caught rather than composed:
a hypothesis declaring an image status; a reading offering model agreement as measurement;
a reading resting on a capability the gap list says is missing; a reading that declared no
status at all; a reading declaring a sixth kind of knowing; a reading anchored to no image;
an alignment against a hypothesis nobody proposed; a plan citing an observation that was
never placed; and a relation that was accepted while its own critique would not vouch for it.
NOTHING in it is nautical to the code. Its twin, `proofs.json`, runs the identical path over
a subject with no vocabulary, no capability and no refusal in common.
prompt: Two moorings, photographed an hour apart. I think the second boat is held more tightly than the first — show me where the pictures bear that out and where they do not.

images.title: the first mooring, from the quay
the second mooring, from the same quay an hour later

hypotheses.statement: the second boat is held more tightly than the first
the older of the two moorings was built for a heavier hull

observations.statement: a thick line runs from the bollard to a cleat near the bow, slack enough to sag between them
the pontoon sits low on the near side, as though something heavy is resting on that end
the rigging is under even tension across all four stays
the fenders are placed at unequal intervals along the hull
two lines cross at the gunwale and take up the load together
the halyard is newer than the rest of the standing gear
the mast leans a degree or two off vertical
something in one of the frames is taut

alignments.statement: the sag in the first mooring's line tells against the proposal at least as much as for it
two lines sharing the load is what being held tightly would look like
the crossing is what you would expect if a blow were forecast

contrast_plans.statement: set the single sagging line of the first mooring against the crossed pair of the second
contrast_plans.because: both are the same job done two ways, and the difference should be legible in the lines alone

contrast_plans.statement: compare how far each pontoon rides above the water
contrast_plans.because: a difference in freeboard would say more about the load than the lines do

accepted_relations.statement: the second mooring carries its load across two lines where the first carries it across one
the second boat is held more tightly than the first
the near cleat takes more of the load than the far one

rejected_relations.statement: the first mooring is older than the second

critiques.because: both frames were read for the same thing and both readings name the same count
the geometry measures one line's sag; the boat's hold is a different quantity and nothing computed it
nothing in either frame dates anything
a critique of a relation that was never proposed

observables.statement: the height of the pontoon deck above the waterline, in pixels
how far the surface has weathered, against a reference
the share of the load taken at each attachment

capability_gaps.why: nothing in this system dates a surface from a photograph
no producer estimates a force from a still frame
nothing here reads the air, and no question in this inquiry asked it to
